evals.prompt: Our editors publish in Optimizely and then ping us on Slack because the site still shows the old copy 20 minutes later. We're on Next.js 15 App Router deployed to Optimizely frontend hosting, three instances. Can you sort out the caching properly?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a missing on-demand revalidation path, not a reason to lower the revalidate interval. Should establish the deployment target as Optimizely frontend hosting and note that three instances require a shared Redis cache handler (cacheHandler in next.config.mjs with an absolute path, cacheMaxMemorySize: 0), because the default filesystem ISR cache is per-instance. Should read references/optimizely-frontend-hosting.md. Should set up: tagged cached fetches via unstable_cache, a webhook receiver at a route like /api/revalidate validating the x-api-key header against OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_CALLBACK_APIKEY, docId parsing in the form {contentKey}_{locale}_{status}, an uncached Graph query to resolve the content key to a URL, revalidateTag plus revalidatePath, and a CDN purge via the Cloud Platform Services edge-cache purge endpoint. Should register the webhook against the Graph origin's /api/webhooks with Basic auth (APP_KEY:SECRET) and a filter on status Published, ideally idempotently from instrumentation.ts. Must derive the origin from OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_GATEWAY (which already includes /content/v2) rather than appending /api/webhooks to it. Should mention filtering the _N_T_/layout tag and namespacing cache keys with OPTIMIZELY_DXP_DEPLOYMENT_ID. Should keep a long revalidate interval as a fallback.

evals.prompt: What revalidate values should I use for my content types? I have ArticlePage, LandingPage, a NavigationSettings singleton, a HeroBlock and a CtaBlock that get reused all over, and a blog index page. Next.js 16, hosted on Vercel.
evals.expected_output: Should give a per-content-type table rather than one global number, roughly: articles/landing pages ~1 hour, navigation/settings ~1 day, shared blocks ~1 hour, listing/index pages ~15 minutes. Should stress that the intervals are only a self-healing fallback and that cache tags are the real mechanism. Should explain that HeroBlock and CtaBlock have no URL of their own, so revalidatePath cannot invalidate the pages embedding them - tags are required. Should propose a consistent tag vocabulary such as optimizely:content:{key}, optimizely:type:{TypeName}, and optimizely:nav. Because the project is Next.js 16, should use 'use cache' with cacheTag/cacheLife rather than unstable_cache, and must state that this requires cacheComponents: true in next.config. Should map the intervals onto cacheLife profiles (hours, days, default) rather than passing raw seconds, and offer a custom cacheLife profile for anything the built-ins don't cover. Must warn that under cacheComponents, route segment exports of revalidate, dynamic, or fetchCache are build errors, so the interval lives in cacheLife() instead. Must note that revalidateTag takes a cache profile as a second argument in Next.js 16 (e.g. revalidateTag(tag, 'max')). Should note Vercel needs no custom cache handler and purges its edge automatically, and should warn about registering the webhook against the stable production domain rather than a preview URL, and about Deployment Protection blocking inbound webhooks.

evals.prompt: I added `export const revalidate = 3600` to app/[...slug]/page.tsx and set up the Optimizely Graph webhook, but nothing ever updates and I don't even see the webhook hitting my app. Self-hosted in Kubernetes with 4 pods behind an nginx ingress.
evals.expected_output: Should run a systematic diagnosis rather than guessing. Should check that the route is actually static in the next build output (dot/ISR rather than f Dynamic) and explain that reading headers(), cookies(), or searchParams silently opts the route out of static generation, with dynamic = 'error' to surface the opt-out at build time and isolating request-dependent parts in Suspense as the fix. Should verify the webhook is registered by GETting /api/webhooks at the Graph origin with Basic auth, deriving that origin from OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_GATEWAY rather than appending to it, and check for duplicates or stale entries pointing at a dead hostname. Should have the user POST a synthetic payload with the x-api-key header to confirm the route returns 200, and without it to confirm 401. Should identify that 4 pods without a shared cache handler is a second, independent bug: the default filesystem cache is per-pod, so revalidation only affects the pod that received the webhook. Should point to references/portable-hosting.md and provide the plain Redis cache handler (no Azure dependencies) plus cacheHandler/cacheMaxMemorySize config. Should mention that next dev ignores cacheHandler so verification requires next build && next start, and that the _N_T_/layout tag must be filtered.

evals.prompt: Write me the revalidation webhook endpoint for our Optimizely site. Next.js 15, app router, self-hosted single container behind Cloudflare.
evals.expected_output: Should produce a POST route handler (e.g. app/api/revalidate/route.ts) with export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'. Should validate the x-api-key header against OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_CALLBACK_APIKEY and return 401 otherwise. Should ignore non-'doc' subjects and non-updated/expired/deleted actions by returning 200 with a skipped flag, explaining that non-2xx responses cause Graph retry storms. Should parse docId as {contentKey}_{locale}_{status}. Should resolve the content key to a URL and type via a Graph query to the /content/v2 endpoint with Authorization: epi-single ${OPTIMIZELY_GRAPH_SINGLE_KEY} and cache: 'no-store', with a request timeout so a slow Graph cannot turn into a webhook timeout. Should call revalidateTag for the content and type tags and revalidatePath for the resolved path, and should include the stripTrailingSlash helper it uses rather than leaving it undefined, preserving '/' as-is. Should add a Cloudflare purge_cache call because revalidating Next.js does not clear the CDN, and note that purge must target the public URL. Should say a single container needs no Redis cache handler, and give the manual curl registration against the Graph origin's /api/webhooks with the Published status filter. Should use single-argument revalidateTag since this is Next.js 15. Should handle deletes where URL resolution returns nothing, log empty resolutions, and mention Graph eventual consistency with a single retry.

evals.prompt: When an editor deletes or unpublishes a page, our blog index still lists it and the old URL still renders until the next day. Publishes work fine. Next.js 15 on DXP behind the Optimizely CDN.
evals.expected_output: Should explain that a deleted page has no URL left to resolve, so the Graph lookup legitimately returns nothing and the handler must not treat that as an error or return a non-2xx (which would trigger Graph retries). Crucially, should recognise that this breaks every targeted invalidation, not just the path one: with no resolved content there is no type either, so a handler that guards its revalidateTag calls behind the resolved content silently does nothing at all and still answers revalidated: true. Should therefore add an explicit branch for null resolution rather than only logging it - a site-wide revalidatePath('/', 'layout') (or a coarse tag on Next 16 with cacheComponents), justified by deletes being far rarer than publishes, with a key-to-path index offered as the option for when broad purges are too costly. Should distinguish unpublish from hard delete: an expired document is still in Graph under a non-Published status, so a status-agnostic resolve query recovers the path and type and keeps the targeted path. Should revalidate the content-key tag unconditionally. Should say to verify by caching the page first, then deleting, then re-requesting, since a URL that 404s was possibly never cached. Should identify that 'the old URL still renders' is a CDN problem as well as an ISR one: on DXP the edge cache must be purged explicitly against the public hostname from OPTIMIZELY_SITE_HOSTNAME, not the absolute URL Graph returns and not an internal container URL. Should check that the webhook subscribes to the deleted and expired actions, not just updated, and note that expired is driven by the CMS StopPublish field. Should point to references/optimizely-frontend-hosting.md for the purge implementation.

evals.prompt: We're migrating to Next.js 16 and turning on cacheComponents. We run 6 replicas in ECS. We already have a Redis cache-handler.mjs wired up via cacheHandler in next.config and it works today on 15. What do we need to change for ISR to keep working?
evals.expected_output: Should identify the central trap: 'use cache' entries do not go through the legacy cacheHandler, so the existing handler will keep loading while silently caching none of the new data, leaving 6 replicas with divergent in-memory caches. Should explain that Next.js 16 uses the cacheHandlers config key (cacheHandlers.default) with a different five-method interface: get(cacheKey, softTags), set(cacheKey, pendingEntry), refreshTags(), getExpiration(tags), and updateTags(tags, durations). Should note that CacheEntry.value is a ReadableStream that must be drained on write and reconstructed on read, and that invalidation is timestamp-based (updateTags records when a tag was invalidated, get compares against the entry timestamp) rather than delete-based, which is what makes it work across instances via refreshTags. Should warn that get() must never throw because Next.js does not wrap it. Should also require removing route segment exports of revalidate, dynamic, and fetchCache since they are build errors under cacheComponents, moving intervals into cacheLife(), and updating revalidateTag calls to pass a profile such as 'max'. Should point to references/nextjs-16-cache-components.md.
